title: Utility Services Terms: Flat Service Lines, Package Fee Lines and Meter Test Fees
content:
# Flat and Package Lines — Utility Services Program

## Terms in force

**F1.** Flat and package lines post only while the account is active or in final billing, as the system record of the account shows.

**F2.** Each covered flat service — trash, pest control and stormwater — and the billing administration fee post once per billing period at the program's monthly amount. A flat amount of $0.00 posts no line.

**F3.** On the All-Inclusive Utility Package the monthly package fee posts once per period instead of every flat and usage line.

**F4.** On the All-Inclusive Utility Package, usage within the allowance is never billed and unused allowance never carries over to another period.

**F5.** A meter test fee line posts only for a resident-requested meter test that finds the meter within the program's accuracy tolerance.

## Terms no longer in force

The following terms have been superseded and are **no longer in force**:

1. The term that flat amounts, the package fee and the package allowances are prorated for a partial first or last month by days of responsibility over the actual days of the period, rounded half up to the cent (allowances to three decimals).
2. The term that usage of water, gas or electricity above its prorated allowance is billed as an overage line at the submetered rate times the package overage multiplier, water overage also carrying the sewer rate.

## Which lines a period carries

| Program | Lines of a period under F2 and F3 |
|---|---|
| Any program other than the All-Inclusive Utility Package | one line for each covered flat service and one for the billing administration fee, except that a $0.00 amount posts no line |
| All-Inclusive Utility Package | one package fee line, in place of every flat and usage line |

*Example (hypothetical package month):* a household on the All-Inclusive Utility Package uses less water than its monthly water allowance. The unused water is not billed and does not carry over to the next month.

*Example (hypothetical meter test):* a resident asks for a meter test. When the test finds the meter within the program's tolerance, a meter test fee line posts; when it does not, F5 posts no fee line.
